title: B2 'Killed' Memory Issue
body:
> What is your rclone version (eg output from `rclone -V`)

rclone v1.28

> Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)

Centos 6 64bit

> Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)

Backblaze B2

> The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

rclone -v sync backups/daily.0/ backb:$(date +%Y-%m)/websites/ --log-file rclonelog

> A log from the command with the `-v` flag (eg output from `rclone -v copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

`tail -10 rclonelog`

> 2016/04/18 12:19:23
> Transferred:            0 Bytes (   0.00 kByte/s)
> Errors:                 0
> Checks:                 0
> Transferred:            0
> Elapsed time:        6m2s
> 
> 2016/04/18 12:19:26 exampledomain.com/images/slideshow/upd-img2_thumb.jpg: Warning: File found with same name but different case on Local file system at /var/backups/daily.0
> 2016/04/18 12:19:26 exampledomain.com/images/slideshow/upd-img3_thumb.jpg: Warning: File found with same name but different case on Local file system at /var/backups/daily.0
> 2016/04/18 12:19:38 example2.com/media/mod_languages/images/si_lk.gif: Warning: File found with same name but different case on Local file system at /var/backups/daily.0

However, the 'killed' error appears in the terminal which launched the rclone process, always around the 6 minute mark, for example:
`-bash-4.1$ rclone -v sync backups/daily.0/ backb:$(date +%Y-%m)/websites/ --log-file rclonelog`
`Killed`
`-bash-4.1$`

Memory log, from beginning of launching to end (I cut out some times in between here) :

> Mon Apr 18 12:13:01 BST 2016
>          1877 M total memory
>           204 M used memory
>            29 M active memory
>            77 M inactive memory

>           439 M inactive memory
>            59 M free memory
>             2 M buffer memory
> 
> Mon Apr 18 12:21:02 BST 2016
>          1877 M total memory
>           161 M used memory
>            13 M active memory
>            50 M inactive memory
>          1715 M free memory
>             5 M buffer memory

It seems to crash before uploading any files at all no matter what I do, always just from reading all the files in the backup directory. What could be causing this issue and how could I get around it? I'm guessing it's storing lots of files into memory or something along those lines. There is literally tens of thousands of files.

Adding `--drive-chunk-size 128M` as an argument did nothing also.
